title: fix(pocket3d): start and exit picks for 3D Pocket
body:
## What changed

This is slice 3 of #3329: the 3D Pocket only. The 3D Pocket now takes a start point and an exit point. Its capability is the existing `PickCapability::Region` (the descent place of the first pass, and the end of the last pass). The picks seat the passes that the strategy already planned on each level. They never re-order the passes.

- Motion: `crates/motion/src/machining3d/level_seam.rs` (the seat laws and the refusals), `level_columns.rs` (the exact column law), `picked.rs` (`pocket3d_picked`, the plain or offset-shell ladder with "Do not touch" items, seated). The ladder gets one `picks` argument; each old caller passes `None`.
- `ladder.rs` gets smaller (441 lines, was 444): `mask_center` moves to `rest.rs`, unchanged.
- App: `OpType::Pocket3D => PickCapability::Region`; the 3D Pocket arm of `generate` calls `pocket3d_picked` only when a pick is set; `pick_kinds` refuses a pick under Adaptive and with Rest roughing; the MCP `edit_operation` schema names the region kind.

The title uses `fix`, because the issue has the `bug` label.

### Behaviour

- **Start:** on each level, the first ring of the first pass starts at its point nearest the start point. It cuts its whole lap back to that point. Then it runs on along its own cut, in its own direction, to its old start. From there the level is the automatic path, move for move: no link changes.
- **Start on zigzag rows:** an open row chain starts at its end nearest the start point (the chain runs the other way). Rows cut both ways, so the reversed chain cuts the same mix.
- **Exit:** on each level, the last ring of the last pass laps from its own start as before. Then it runs on along its own cut to its point nearest the exit point. An open zigzag chain ends at its end nearest the exit point. The operation's exit is the end of the last pass of the last level that cuts.
- **A level of one ring with the two picks:** the lap from the start point runs on straight to the exit point.
- A run-on re-traces a cut at the same depth. It removes no new material.
- The descent at the new start goes through the ladder's own entry rule (helix, ramp, arc, plunge and their stand-ins).
- The ladder reads the X and Y of a pick. A pick with a Z gets one note (`PICK_Z_UNREAD`).
- A ring of a ring strategy is never reversed (climb would become conventional cutting). The passes are never re-ordered (the ring order is the engagement law).
- With no pick, the output is the automatic path, byte for byte.

### Refusals (by name, never moved)

- A start point farther than 1.5 tool diameters from the start of the first pass of a level: `start point (x, y): the first pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z starts at (...), d mm from it, farther than the L mm ...`.
- A descent that the entry rule puts farther than that reach from the start point: `start point (x, y): the entry rule at Z z finds no room for its motion at the start point and descends at (...)`.
- An exit point farther than that reach from the end of the operation: `exit point (x, y): the last pass of the 3D Pocket at Z z ends at (...)`.
- A pick on a level that the Adaptive (HSM) plan spirals (its own entry bore and proved arcs).
- In the application, at the edit: a pick under the Adaptive strategy, and a pick with Rest roughing on.
- A plunge or retract column at a point that a pick moved that comes within the tool radius (less 0.01 mm) of the part.
  - The check is exact: each facet is clipped to the half-space above the column's foot, then `stock_sim::dist_seg_tri` measures the distance from the column's axis segment to what is left. There is no sampling. A distance that is not a number is a hit.
  - The moved points: the new start of a re-seated ring, the new end of a run-on, both ends of a reversed chain, and the descent place that the entry rule chose.
  - The islands law of the ladder already keeps each ring point clear above its level, so no ladder fixture reaches this refusal. It is a second, independent check, pinned by a unit test.

### Same-region rule

The start and the exit act on different passes of a level: the first pass and the last pass. Where a level has one pass, the two picks act on one ring: the lap from the start point runs on to the exit point (a re-trace, simple and safe). Where that one pass is an open chain, the exit is not moved: the exit reach law then refuses an exit that the chain does not end near.

### Mutation table

Each mutation was applied alone, then `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib level_seam` and `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pocket3d_pass_start picks` ran (M11: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test start_exit_shared pocket3d`).

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | No column law (`columns` checks no point) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M2 | Column law tests only the two ends of the column (no segment distance) | RED: `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot` |
| M3 | No start reach law | RED: `a_start_beyond_the_first_pass_is_refused_with_its_level`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M4 | No exit reach law | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M5 | No descent law | RED: `a_descent_far_from_the_start_point_is_refused`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M6 | No one-ring run-on from the start to the exit | RED: `a_level_of_one_ring_laps_from_the_start_and_runs_on_to_the_exit` |
| M7 | No run back to the old start after the re-seat | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends` |
| M8 | No exit run-on | RED: `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends`, `an_exit_pick_ends_the_operation_on_the_last_ring` |
| M9 | No zigzag reversal | RED: `zigzag_rows_start_at_their_end_nearest_the_start_point`, `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M10 | No refusal of an HSM level | RED: `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` |
| M11 | No application refusal (Adaptive, Rest roughing) | RED: `pocket3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` |

## Readings

- Motion fixture (40 mm square pocket, 10 mm island, tool radius 3, Waterline, plunge entry, Z 8 / 3 / 0): a start at (30, 33) gives the descent of each level at (30, 32.2); the automatic descent is at (32.2, 32.2). An exit at (20, 11) gives the last cut end at (20, 12, 0), and the rise is straight up.
- Zigzag, 39.62 mm pocket, no island: a start at (38, 38) reverses the row chain; each level descends within 1 mm of (36.61, 36.61) (automatic: near (3.01, 3.01)).
- App brick (10 mm block in 40 x 40 stock, `EM-0600-4FL`, Offset rings, Z 6 / 2): a start at (-14, 10) gives each descent at (-12.961, 11.095) (automatic: (-12.636, 11.502)). An exit at (10, -21) gives the last cut end at (10, -19.99, 2).
- Reach with the 6 mm mill: 9 mm.

## Pinning tests

`camcraft-motion`, `tests/pocket3d_pass_start.rs`, new module `pocket3d_pass_start/picks.rs` (joins the existing suite, no new test binary):
- `no_pick_is_the_automatic_ladder_byte_for_byte` (Waterline, Offset rings, Zigzag, Auto; plain and offset shell)
- `a_start_pick_seats_the_first_ring_of_every_level` (also: the unread Z is said once)
- `an_exit_pick_ends_the_operation_on_the_last_ring` (exit alone, and start with exit)
- `zigzag_rows_start_at_their_end_nearest_the_start_point`
- `an_impossible_pick_is_refused_by_name` (start, exit, descent, HSM level)

Each picked path is gouge-checked at every cut move, sampled each 0.25 mm along its length (the island, the footprint, the floor). Each also cuts all that the automatic path cuts, level by level (a 0.5 mm grid of the swept tool disc).

`camcraft-motion` lib, `machining3d/level_seam_tests.rs`:
- `the_column_law_is_exact_above_the_foot`
- `a_level_of_one_ring_laps_from_the_start_and_runs_on_to_the_exit`
- `a_chain_keeps_its_links_and_moves_only_its_ends`
- `a_start_beyond_the_first_pass_is_refused_with_its_level`
- `a_descent_far_from_the_start_point_is_refused`

`camcraft-app`, `tests/start_exit_shared.rs`, new module `start_exit_shared/pocket3d.rs`:
- `pocket3d_starts_at_the_picked_point_and_ends_at_the_picked_exit` (also: no pick gives the automatic path again; gouge pin each 0.25 mm)
- `pocket3d_refuses_an_impossible_pick_by_name` (generation, and MCP edits under Adaptive and Rest roughing)
- `pocket3d_picks_ride_edit_operation_and_undo_restores_them` (MCP `edit_operation`, `get_job`, undo, redo, the schema text)
- Updated: `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (3D Pocket is `Region`), `a_pick_on_a_kind_that_does_not_take_it_names_the_kind_and_the_reason` (Trace replaces 3D Pocket as the example of a kind that takes no pick).

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The UI has no 3D Pocket start / exit rows yet. The picks are set through MCP `edit_operation` and the project file, the same as the 5-axis and the Deburr slices. The "Not taken" lines of the 3D Pocket go away.
- The Trochoidal method and the rotary wrap (`pocket3d_air_split`) take no pick: the first is Adaptive (refused), the second is not the 3D Pocket arm.
- The column refusal is not reached through the ladder (see above); the unit test pins it.

## Remaining kinds of #3329

None after this PR, #4168 (Deburr) and the 3D Finish PR (in work). The issue closes when all three slices merge, so this PR says `Refs #3329`.

## Gate

All runs are on head `8ce7f2dbb1b7dcc45a727d4b2c7e9d147d93a766` (the merge of `origin/main` with #4168, the Deburr slice; both sides kept in `pick_kinds.rs`, `start_exit_shared.rs` and `mcp/tools.rs`). The log is `scratchpad/gates/3329c-8ce7f2dbb.log`, and its first line is the head SHA.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 226 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (35.0 min). This includes `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: pocket3d_pass_start`, `app suites: lib`, `app suites: start_exit_shared` (46 tests, the Deburr module too), `app suites: pocket3d_pass_start`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` and `first_part_programs`.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (7.6 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: exit 0.
- The pre-merge head `bf9669e73` had the same gate green (226 steps, light 6 steps).
- The PR merges cleanly with the current `main` (`git merge-tree`).

No heavy step: this is a P2 PR.

Changelog: 3D Pocket takes a start point and an exit point: each level descends on its first ring at the point nearest the start (zigzag rows from their nearer end) and the operation ends on its last ring at the point nearest the exit; an impossible pick, Adaptive and Rest roughing are refused by name.
